the calsequestration of Ca(2+), as well as the Ca(2+)/Ca(2+)-dependent regulation of Ca(2+)/Mg(2+)-ATPase, are affected by fiber type transitions and age-related changes.
calsequestrins, junctins and triadins are not only involved in the regulation of Ca(2+), but also in the maintenance and modulation of the supramolecular calseqestrin complex.
calsequestrins are the key players in the supramolecular calsequestirn complex and that their expression is tightly regulated during muscle fiber development and aging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calsequestrins are the central element of the junctional SR, and that calsequestrain binding to other proteins of the SR is affected by the relative expression of these proteins.
calsequestrins are the key players of the supramolecular calsequestrin complex, which is composed of calsequestrine, junctin, triadin, and ryanodine receptors.
calsequestrins, junctins, triadins and ryanodine receptors are not simply co-localized in the junctional membrane of the sarcoplamic reticulum but form a supramolecular complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calsequestration of calcium by calsequestrins is a complex process that is affected by the expression and isoform shifting of the proteins involved.
the supramolecular calsequestin complex is not a fixed structure, but can be altered by physiological stimuli, including fiber type transitions, aging and development.
